label: Pre-Christian Slavic religion
description: The pre-Christian Slavic religion. The gods Perun, Veles, Svarog, Dazhbog, Khors, Stribog, and Mokosh are worshipped. The evidence is archaeological and reconstructed (no contemporary literary sources).

label: The 980 CE 'destruction of the idols'
description: The pagan ruler Vladimir of Kiev orders the destruction of the pagan idols, including the great wooden idol of Perun. This is the oldest attested event in the Slavic pantheon's history.

label: The Primary Chronicle
description: The Primary Chronicle (Latopis povest' vremen'nykh let) is composed. It names the Kiev pantheon (Perun, Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog, Veles, Mokosh) and describes the 980 'destruction of the idols'.

label: The 'Tales of the Destruction of the Idols'
description: The 'Tale of the Destruction of the Idols' (Skazanie o razrushenii idolov) and other later chronicles retell the 980 event and the pagan pantheon in detail.

label: Ethnographic collection
description: 19th-20th c. ethnographers (Vsevolod Miller, Vasily Ivanov, etc.) collect folk survivals of the pre-Christian religion: the 'drowning of Marzanna', the 'Kupala' night, the 'Veles-day', the folk gods (Lada, Morana, Zorya).
